Yes, age at orchiopexy can affect the survival and fertility potential of the testis in cases of undescended testes. 

Orchiopexy, the surgical procedure to move an undescended testis into the scrotum, is most effective when performed before the age of 1 year, preferably between 6-12 months. Early intervention can help minimize potential damage to the testis from increased temperature, reduce the risk of testicular cancer, and improve fertility prospects.

Delayed orchiopexy, especially after 2-3 years of age, may result in lower survival rates of the testis, decreased fertility potential, and increased risk of testicular atrophy or cancer. 

The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends orchiopexy by 12-18 months of age for optimal outcomes.
